clue.text: Maybe, Harry and Fred featured in report?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the cricketer's surname is said out loud

parts.note: Fred Trueman was a famous English fast bowler in cricket

explanation.surface: A question about whether two men called Harry and Fred appeared in some written report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks Harry as an example: Harry S Truman, US president. 'Featured in report' says Fred Trueman's surname, spoken, gives the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S Truman was the 33rd US president, one famous bearer of the first name.

clue.text: Persistence from criminal type in act ignoring first sign of police

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring means a letter is left out of the word type
first sign of picks the opening letter of the word police

explanation.surface: Someone's determination is traced back to a crook caught red-handed, the police not getting a look in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring first sign of police' drops P from TYPE, leaving TYE; 'criminal' rearranges TYE + IN + ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is the quality of holding on doggedly, a synonym for persistence.

clue.text: Posh learner into fancy new Diy? That's not easy to handle

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

indicators.note: into says the learner letter goes inside the rearranged letters
fancy here means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A snooty novice gets into a do-it-yourself project and finds it hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges NEW + DIY to NWIEDY; 'into' puts L inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwieldy is awkward and cumbersome to manage or carry.

clue.text: A poet carrying nothing on train?

indicators.note: carrying means the poet word holds the nothing letter inside it

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A poet with empty pockets sitting on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' puts O inside BARD to give BOARD, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard means being on a vehicle such as a train, ship or plane; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Part of speech, one before time producing excessive words

indicators.note: before says the numeral comes ahead of the period of time

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
I is the Roman numeral one
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Grammar talk about a part of speech that goes on too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbiage is wordiness, using far more language than needed.

clue.text: Check section in contested item

indicators.note: section in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An auditor checks part of a disputed entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to check and correct it.

clue.text: Talk spitefully about small amount taken in by sponsor largely

indicators.note: taken in by means the small amount goes inside the shortened sponsor word
largely means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a backer is a sponsor
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: Gossiping nastily about a tiny sum swallowed up by a patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' cuts BACKER to BACKE; 'taken in by' puts BIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To backbite is to speak ill of someone behind their back.

clue.text: A person lacking sign of truth and without principles

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is taken out of the person word

parts.note: a mortal is a human, a person

indicators.note: sign of picks the opening letter of the word truth

explanation.surface: Someone who never shows a trace of honesty is unprincipled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking sign of truth' drops T from MORTAL, leaving MORAL after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone with no moral sense, indifferent to right and wrong.

clue.text: Crime writer giving no introduction about European city

indicators.note: about says the shortened name goes around the European letter
no introduction means the writer's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse crime novels

explanation.surface: A crime novelist, without any preamble, writes about a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No introduction' trims DEXTER to EXTER; 'about' wraps it round E. EXETER is a cathedral city in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a city in south-west England, the county town of Devon.

clue.text: Element carrying weight for a law giver?

indicators.note: carrying means the element word holds the weight letters inside

parts.note: neon is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A chemical element bearing a load stands in for a lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' puts WT inside NEON after NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton formulated the laws of motion and gravitation, so he gave physics its laws.

clue.text: Reveal date is with actress

parts.note: Glenn Close is an American actress

explanation.surface: A gossip column revealing who a famous actress is dating.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known or expose something hidden.

clue.text: With no end of fun, Ben and Julie devised timely celebration

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged
with no means a letter is removed from the name Ben
end of picks the last letter of the word fun

explanation.surface: Two people, Ben and Julie, plan a party that is no fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no end of fun' drops N from BEN, leaving BE; 'devised' rearranges BE + JULIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jubilee is an anniversary celebration held at a set time, such as a 25th or 50th year.

clue.text: Definite chapter by poet excised

parts.note: Edward Lear was a nonsense poet
excised means cut out

explanation.surface: A firm decision that a chapter by some poet has been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear-cut means sharply defined and certain, leaving no doubt.

clue.text: A part of school outfit not right? It's brightly lit

indicators.note: not means the right letter is left out of the jacket word

parts.note: a blazer is a jacket worn as school uniform

explanation.surface: A school uniform item is called wrong, while something nearby glows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' drops R from BLAZER, leaving BLAZE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze means on fire or shining with light.

clue.text: Evasive line maybe

explanation.surface: A slanted remark about a line.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblique answer avoids the point, being indirect; an oblique is also a slanting stroke, a line.

clue.text: Stir also around centre of pudding

indicators.note: around means the also word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word pudding

explanation.surface: Instructions for a cook to stir the middle of a pudding as well.
explanation.walkthrough: PUDDING has seven letters, so its centre is D; 'around' places TOO round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, as is a stir.

clue.text: Leaders of kingdom in big bother unifying this unknown communal settlement

indicators.note: leaders of picks the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: Z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Heads of a kingdom in serious trouble unite to form a new collective community.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaders run from 'kingdom' to 'this', giving KIBBUT, before Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A kibbutz is a collective farm or settlement in Israel.

clue.text: Tip in support of English players

parts.note: for means in favour of
a cast is the group of players in a show

explanation.surface: A recommendation backing English actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip in racing or finance is a prediction, a forecast of what will win.

clue.text: Venomous review of live turn

indicators.note: a review goes over something again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scathing critique of a performer's live act.
explanation.definitionFit: Virulent means poisonous or bitterly hostile.

clue.text: Unsophisticated former PM given a favourable slant

parts.note: Alec Douglas-Home was British Prime Minister 1963 to 1964
spun means presented with spin, a favourable slant

explanation.surface: A simple ex-premier whose record has been spun favourably.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and simple, like cloth woven at home.

clue.text: Plant getting award among all I cultivated

indicators.note: among means the award goes inside the rearranged letters
cultivated suggests something worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A gardener wins a prize for a plant they grew themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' rearranges ALL + I to LLIA; 'among' puts OBE after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden plant, often blue, used in borders.

clue.text: One might be found sheltering in window in off-licence?

definitions.text: One might be found sheltering in window in off-licence?

indicators.note: sheltering in means the answer is tucked away inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A drinker takes cover in a liquor shop's doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'window in off'; the whole clue also pictures a drinker found at an off-licence, a British shop selling alcohol to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drinker of cheap wine, who might well hang about a liquor shop.

clue.text: Bird with a sound I missed over top of tree

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above what follows
missed means the letter I is left out of the sound word

parts.note: a voice is a sound
taken as written

indicators.note: top of picks the opening letter of the word tree

explanation.surface: A bird calls out but misses, flying above the treetop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I missed' drops I from VOICE, leaving VOCE; in a down clue 'over' places A + VOCE above T.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Very quick throw around yard

indicators.note: around means the throw word goes round the yard letter

parts.note: to fling is to throw

explanation.surface: A fast pitch thrown around the backyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying means extremely fast, as in a flying visit.

clue.text: Fight close to office causing predicament

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: close to picks the last letter of the word office

explanation.surface: A brawl near the workplace lands someone in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward or difficult situation.

clue.text: Discharge, a common feature in court?

explanation.surface: A firing of weapons happening in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley is a discharge of many guns at once; in tennis it is a shot hit before the ball bounces on the court.

clue.text: Unwelcome reason for having a flat?

definitions.text: Unwelcome reason for having a flat?

parts.words: Unwelcome reason for having a flat?
parts.note: looks like a housing matter, but the flat is a deflated tyre and the reason is a hole in it

explanation.definitionFit: A puncture is a small hole that lets the air out of a tyre, leaving it flat.

clue.text: A largely genuine district

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood described as mostly authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district.

clue.text: Honourable code in church competition? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means the competition word loses its first letter

parts.note: rivalry means competition

explanation.surface: A church contest where good manners matter, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' drops R from RIVALRY, leaving IVALRY after CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry was the medieval knightly code of honour and courtesy.

clue.text: Feign slap

explanation.surface: Pretending to hit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up a story is to invent or feign it; slap is theatrical slang for greasepaint and cosmetics.

clue.text: No generous sort broadcast that dig about wife

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the wife letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stingy man complains on air about a dig at his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges THAT + DIG to TIGHTAD; 'about' puts it round W.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightwad is a miser, someone who hates spending money.

clue.text: On radio, cookery writer is overwhelmed

indicators.note: on radio means the writer's name is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Mrs Isabella Beeton wrote a famous Victorian book of household management and recipes

explanation.surface: A celebrity cook is defeated during a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten is to be defeated or overcome.
